data_cache.earnings_method: RESOLVED 2026-07-28 (G20): reliable method is yfinance get_earnings -> take the latest quarterly reportedDate and add ~91 days for the next print; cross-check near-dated names against the FMP earnings-calendar endpoint (works on the current plan for the calendar range query; the per-symbol earnings-company endpoint is plan-blocked). yfinance's own earnings-calendar endpoint remains unreliable -- do not use it.
data_cache.beta_method: RESOLVED 2026-07-28 (G15): betas computed vs SMH (the book's true factor, not SPX) from 20 daily returns, 25 Jun - 24 Jul 2026. CAVEAT: a 20-observation window carries wide standard errors -- treat these as ordinal (which names are high- vs low-beta) rather than precise point estimates, and refresh to a 60-day window on the next deep run. No name now defaults to 1.0. TTL 30 days; refresh after 2026-08-27.
data_cache.sentiment_method: RESOLVED-IN-PART 2026-07-28 (G17). Findings: (a) 52-week high/low from WEEKLY bars is EXACT, not an approximation -- a weekly high is by construction the max of that week's daily highs, so the 52wk range component never had an error; (b) RSI14 must use TRUE DAILY closes -- the weekly-aggregated version read 53.12 against a true daily 35.81, a 17.3-point error that materially misstated the composite; (c) the 125-day MA still uses weekly closes, a genuine but small smoothing approximation. METHOD: indices auto-aggregate to weekly for period>=3mo; use period='1mo' with at most 3 symbols per call to force daily bars. RSI14 needs only 15 daily closes, so one 1mo call suffices.

cache_policy.rationale: A quick run was costing ~119KB of raw API payload (~33k tokens), of which 18 of 27 calls were avoidable. ATR20, betas and earnings dates are slow-moving; re-pulling them every run is the single largest waste.
cache_policy.refresh_rule: On a QUICK run, read every cache as-is; refresh nothing. On a DEEP run, refresh only entries whose TTL has expired. ATR20 over a 20-day window drifts roughly 5% per week -- weekly refresh is ample, and a stale ATR makes stops slightly wide, which is the safe direction to be wrong.
cache_policy.price_source_rule: Live prices: use yfinance get_stock_price (232 chars/symbol). Use INDmoney get_us_stocks_details (726 chars/symbol, 3.1x heavier) ONLY when market_session is pre-open and ext_hr_live_price is genuinely needed. get_stock_price already carries price, prev_close and day high/low -- everything the stop framework consumes.
cache_policy.session_reuse: Do not re-pull prices for the same symbol within 20 minutes unless the user asks for a fresh check or a stop level is being placed.
